subject: Re: Rerank model validation — BrightCart discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@brightcart.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-09T17:12:00-08:00
Subject: Rerank model validation — initial post-call recap

Hi Priya / Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Key business problem: BrightCart wants to improve on-site search relevance for long-tail queries and promotional ranking (goal: measurable lift in NDCG@10 and MRR while avoiding surface-level clickbait regressions).
- What we heard: small but high-value product categories; heavy seasonal spikes; existing infra returns a candidate set + engineered score that you'd like to augment with an ML reranker.

Our suggested initial scope (pilot): 
1) Run offline evaluation comparing 3 candidate rerank approaches (see table below):
   - xglm-4b-quant (fast, low cost)
   - rwd-rank-7b (our recommended medium-size reranker — balanced precision/latency)
   - open-bert-rerank-bert-large (strong baseline)
2) Use your annotated judgment set (~5k queries) + click-derived implicit labels for MRR/NDCG; run lightweight calibration.
3) A/B plan for on-site experiment: 2-week bake + priority-based rollout (1% -> 5% -> 20%).

Deliverables we can produce by next Tue (2027-02-16):
- Benchmarks: NDCG/MRR CSV + latency/cost per request
- Prompt set + deterministic rerank prompt templates
- Canary A/B config and guardrails for quality regression (fallback to baseline score if model score delta > threshold)

Could you confirm the accepted evaluation set (judgment file + click log slice), and whether we should include holiday-season traffic in the initial slice? Also flag any redlines on latency: you mentioned a 150 ms p95 budget — can we assume that applies to total extra latency from the reranker?

Attached: proposed prompt_sets_v1.json (starter prompts) — I put a short attachment with templated prompts for reranking.

Thanks — happy to sync on a quick screen share if helpful.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[attachment: prompt_sets_v1.json]

From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@brightcart.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Keller <tom.keller@brightcart.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-09T18:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Rerank model validation — initial post-call recap

Thanks Marcus — that recap matches our notes. A few clarifications from BrightCart: 

- Evaluation set: we'll share 5,200 human judgments (category-weighted) and a 30-day click log sample (UTC: 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-30) — include both.
- Latency: yes, 150 ms p95 is a hard target for the extra hop; if a model exceeds that in lab, we need fallback.
- Success metric: target >= +4% NDCG@10 and +6% MRR vs. current scorer for the judged set; online improvement expectations negotiable.

Please move forward with the three candidate runs. Can you also provide an estimate of per-100k-request cost for each model variant? We'll need that for procurement planning.

Priya
Head of Search & Personalization | BrightCart

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-10T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Rerank model validation — benchmarks and recommended plan

Hi Priya / team — following Marcus' ask, we ran the offline evaluation against your judgment set (attached) and a 30-day click slice. High-level findings: 

- NDCG@10 / MRR (judged set):
  * open-bert-rerank-bert-large: NDCG@10 = 0.432, MRR = 0.391
  * rwd-rank-7b: NDCG@10 = 0.457 (+5.8%), MRR = 0.417 (+6.6%)
  * xglm-4b-quant: NDCG@10 = 0.445 (+3.0%), MRR = 0.402 (+2.8%)

- Latency (p95 extra):
  * open-bert-rerank-bert-large: 210 ms (exceeds 150 ms)
  * rwd-rank-7b: 130 ms (meets target)
  * xglm-4b-quant: 95 ms (well under target)

- Cost (rough unit estimate, per 100k requests):
  * open-bert-rerank-bert-large: ~$1,200
  * rwd-rank-7b: ~$680
  * xglm-4b-quant: ~$320

Notes and concerns: 
- rwd-rank-7b hits your NDCG/MRR targets in offline eval and meets latency. It's our recommended default for the pilot.
- open-bert has slightly lower cost-per-request tradeoffs and higher model quality in other internal benchmarks, but it violates latency SLO in your infra — we'd need batching changes or quantization.
- We observed a small but consistent failure mode for promotional queries (model over-favors promotional badges), which causes precision regressions for a ~4% subset. We propose a quick mitigator: post-score calibration that mixes your baseline engineered score with model score for promo-labeled items (weighting alpha=0.6 baseline / 0.4 model) — this cut regressions to 1.2% in our sim.

Attachments included: ndcg_mrr_results.csv (detailed metrics), prompt_sets_v1.json (prompt templates).

Proposed A/B plan (canary):
- Week 1: 1% traffic, check stability and promo-regressions daily; rollback if regression > 2%
- Week 2: 5% traffic with dedicated monitoring on promotional buckets and top-sellers; run stats test for NDCG and CTR changes
- Week 3: 20% traffic with progressive ramp if all checks pass

Next actions for BrightCart: confirm the eval set delivery link (we used the Drive link below) and sign off on the canary thresholds. After sign-off we can schedule a short kickoff for instrumentation (traces + cost telemetry).

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: ndcg_mrr_results.csv]

Priya / Tom — looping in a short approval note from our side. Thanks Jasmine for the quick turnaround on the runs. We approve the recommended pilot using rwd-rank-7b with the promotion calibration mitigator described above. A few operational asks before kickoff: 

- Instrumentation: please confirm we can get a daily export of the canary bucket click-through metrics and model-score deltas (we'll provide a small telemetry webhook or S3 sink).
- Fallback policy: implement automatic fallback to baseline if model latency > 200 ms or if promotional precision regression in live exceeds 2% for 24h.
- Post-mortem: if we see a regression, require a 48h post-mortem with root cause + remediation plan before re-rolling.

If BrightCart signs off on the thresholds above we can spin up the pilot stack and aim for a Monday production canary (2027-02-14). Marcus — can you confirm the procurement cost estimate and share a draft SOW for the pilot?

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
